Structure is ready. Activity ground truth is the next gate.

Professor review · 3 November 2026

A local, read-only review of the existing 27–29 October model runs, mapped to today's questions. New charts summarize saved outputs; no model has been retrained, no labels inferred, and no source evidence overwritten. The honest conclusion: the repository has a working structure-only selection classifier and most requested chemical features. It has not yet demonstrated a classifier for herbicidal activity in natural products. Strong selection accuracy does not close that scientific gap.
Navigate: Goal assessment · Formula/features · Fair model comparison · Held-out errors · Dimensionality/stress · Labels · Expansion sources · Meeting decisions

1 · Goal assessment

Status is reported by deliverable and evidence. A completion percentage would conceal that implemented software and validated biological prediction are different milestones.
Toxicity profiles and differentiating properties: reusable acquisition, normalization, seven-endpoint structured EPA support, missingness-aware coverage, descriptive comparisons and presentation are implemented. Comparing matched potency across all endpoints and concluding relative safety remain unfinished: aquatic evidence is sparse and study context heterogeneous. Known natural-product–protein binding: reference target/protein/resistance tables and literature context exist. A source-reviewed interaction dataset and validated binding-characterization workflow remain open. Plant-growth inhibition and selection classification do not establish direct protein binding. Safer bioherbicide discovery: features and exploratory models support the path toward the goal. Accepted efficacy, independent validation, non-target hazard profiles and practical follow-up are still needed. No safer candidate or deployment-ready model has been established.
176 prepared compounds in the older evidence presentation. Counts below describe eligible saved evidence, not toxicity potency. Chronic example policies deliberately leave pooled potency medians null. This cohort differs from the 171-compound structural ablations; these source flags never enter structural predictors.

2 · Formula and chemical features

Formula model ≠ element-count-only model. The existing formula representation contains 27 composition predictors: distinct elements, total atoms, other atoms, and counts/fractions for 12 named elements. Isomers can share every formula feature. SMILES supplies connectivity/fingerprints; InChIKey is an identity audit key, never a numeric predictor. Toxicity is not required to derive these predictors.

Implemented Lipinski violation count: MW > 500, RDKit logP > 5, H-bond donors > 5, acceptors > 10. It is an oral-drug screening heuristic, not a herbicidal activity label. Implemented Tice-inspired proxy: MW outside 150–500, logP > 3.5, donors > 3, acceptors outside 2–12, rotatable bonds > 12. Definitions are explicitly RDKit-based; exact reproduction of Tice's original calculators has not been established. The current code does not create a new validated rule set. Synthetic accessibility: Ertl fragment/complexity heuristic through RDKit's bundled SA scorer; lower values suggest easier synthesis, higher harder. Natural extraction, supply, synthesis route, yield and cost require other evidence. Primary SA method. A reasonable next rule experiment: predeclare a shallow model or small rule family, learn thresholds only inside training folds, and validate on independent chemistry/activity labels. Do not choose a cutoff from the complete distributions here and present its resubstitution score as validation.

3 · Fair model comparison

These are the same 171 compounds, 55 selected herbicides / 116 selected natural products, and the same five scaffold folds for all nine profiles and both modes. Positive means membership in the selected-herbicide group. Every predictor is finite in this ablation cohort; zero input values were imputed. Fixed: C=1. Nested: C selected over 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100 within three inner scaffold folds in each outer training set. All reported scores are outer held-out predictions. Choosing a profile after inspecting these scores is still exploratory. No confidence interval or external confirmation is supplied by these runs.

Dashed reference = 0.500: 0.5 ranking/balanced-accuracy reference. Average precision depends on prevalence.
Interpretation: formula + descriptors at fixed C gains only one net selected-herbicide detection over formula alone. Preserving formula outside PCA does not by itself recover the gap. Nested C substantially improves the combined model, suggesting regularization/operating-point behavior matters. These comparisons do not identify a validated biological activity winner.

4 · Inspect held-out errors

Explore saved out-of-fold predictions. At the default 0.50 threshold the confusion counts reproduce the saved reports. Changing the slider explores sensitivity on these same outcomes; selecting a threshold here would need separate validation. Probabilities are uncalibrated selection scores.
A selected natural product called 'herbicide' is a selection error; it is not proof of either herbicidal activity or inactivity.

5 · Dimensionality and stress tests

Formula starts with 27 predictors, descriptors 11, Morgan fingerprints 2,048, and the original combined input 2,086. Variance filtering, scaling and PCA are learned within training folds. PCA retains 95% of training variance; it is unsupervised and may discard predictive low-variance directions. Fingerprint PCA can still leave about a hundred components for fewer than 171 training compounds. Dimensionality is managed, not solved. All fingerprint-containing nested profiles hit the tested C-grid boundary of 100 in every outer fold; this is not evidence of a global optimum.
Twenty shuffled-label controls per representation hover around chance. Removing the largest scaffold changes the cohort (171 → 122), so that stress result is not a same-population model comparison. These checks expose fragility; they do not supply external activity validation.

6 · The label bottleneck

The frozen review export has 157 measurements from 14 assays / 14 publications. The working worksheet has 154 compound rows; 0 have known activity and 0 known origin in the inspected copy. These are source-specific counts, not a census of all research labels. The requested categories overlap. A natural product can be herbicidal. Use separate axes: natural occurrence/provenance and plant activity under an agreed assay policy. A useful future model can predict activity for a known natural product without pretending 'natural' is its opposite class.
Working labels read from analysis/outputs/chembl-researcher-handoff-2026-10-29/reviewed_labels.csv. The notebook never modifies them. Use the tracked analysis/docs/label_review_guide.md to adjudicate publication methods, dose/time/species, inequalities, conflicts and occurrence separately. Unknown or untested is not inactive.

7 · Expansion sources and sequencing

Source pages rechecked 3 November 2026. No bulk collection has been imported by this notebook. A large unlabeled library increases candidate coverage; it does not manufacture reviewed activity ground truth.
Source Suitable next use Current repository gap
HRAC 2026 master list Extend recognized herbicide identities/MoA; XLSX with/without structures Freeze roster and review salts/esters/stereo; not a standardized active/inactive assay dataset
COCONUT downloads Versioned natural-product structure library; page now offers November 2026 CSV/SDF and CC0 release No full import/batch scorer yet; database 'active/inactive' terminology is not herbicidal ground truth
LOTUS primary description, portal Referenced structure–organism relationships for occurrence and literature leads Freeze export/query and review provenance; occurrence does not imply activity; portal content was not text-readable in this check
KNApSAcK Core Targeted metabolite/species/structure searches and references Broader acquisition remains unimplemented; source page restricts redistribution/commercial use without contact; establish an appropriate access/reuse route
Frozen ChEMBL plant assays / PubChem BioAssay literature leads Reviewed comparable actives and tested negatives before broad screening 14 assays acquired; original-paper context and label adjudication still needed
Sequence: agree activity policy → curate diverse actives/tested negatives and natural-occurrence evidence → reserve independent chemical/publication holdouts → evaluate structure models and calibration → freeze a natural-product release → implement bounded batch scoring with identity/provenance/domain checks. HRAC and natural-source enrichment can be prepared now. Claims that a model 'performs well' should use an agreed, independent activity validation criterion, not the selection scores above. The existing candidate command loads the list in memory and uses pairwise similarity; a full-library batch interface is a separate engineering step. See analysis/docs/compound_sources.md for the original dated source assessment and specific assay leads.

data.text/markdown:
8 · Decisions for today

Suggested meeting summary: “We have the structure-only feature/model pipeline, including formula composition, PCA, rule proxies and SA. Formula discriminates our curated groups well, but that is not yet an activity classifier. We have additional measured plant-assay evidence ready for review; the immediate next milestone is a defensible activity/origin training set and independent validation.”
  1. Define the task: prioritize predicting plant activity in natural candidates; maintain natural occurrence as a separate cited label. Is a broad selection diagnostic also useful as a secondary research question?
  2. Agree biological policy: species/weed, pre/post emergence, endpoint, exposure/duration, controls, positive/negative bands, qualifiers and conflicts. What would constitute a useful tested negative?
  3. Choose validation before more model search: reserve publications/chemotypes, agree precision–recall and sensitivity tradeoffs, calibration/domain checks, and what evidence would justify broad candidate screening. Scaffold support matters more than simply reaching a large row count.
  4. Decide the next deliverable: a versioned reviewed-label pilot and its audit, then a held-out activity benchmark. For a rule set, predeclare a small interpretable candidate family and validate it without whole-dataset threshold picking.
  5. Keep the broader goals visible: separate non-target hazard comparison, known binding-interaction curation and practical accessibility from efficacy. None is completed merely by making the candidate library larger.
Readiness: feature extraction ready; internal selection modeling demonstrated, exploratory; new discriminating rule set not validated; biological activity training data requires review; broad natural-product screen waits on validation and batch engineering. This gives concrete finish criteria without inventing a completion percentage or a safety claim.
